key_insight: Predictive triboelectric nanogenerator design requires linking evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay to electrical output across length scales.
engineering_relevance: Connecting materials, interface mechanics and circuit response can guide more reliable mechanical-energy harvesters and self-powered sensors.
method: Review polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials for charging, compliance and durability.
Assess molecular, contact-mechanics, electrostatic and circuit models by their inputs, predictions and validation evidence.
Organise applications by device scale and propose staged validation beyond calibration conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review of model capabilities and experimental validation evidence, but reports no quantitative benchmark or new device-performance result.
watch_item: Prescribed surface charge, idealised geometry and nominal contact-area assumptions can limit predictions under realistic loading.
paper_title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
